trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly SBB Swiss train from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald (approx. 2.5–3 hrs via Interlaken Ost, ~CHF 35–45 with a Swiss Travel Pass or second-class ticket). Check in to Grindelwald Boutique Stay, drop luggage, and freshen up. Take a short stroll around Grindelwald village center to get oriented — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face from the village streets.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald's main street (Dorfstrasse). Window-shop, pick up snacks or groceries from the Coop or Migros supermarket for budget breakfasts during the week. Enjoy a relaxed first evening settling in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 5–10)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pretzel from a kiosk at Interlaken Ost train station during layover (CHF 6–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Coop/Migros supermarket in Grindelwald — pick up pasta, bread, cheese, and cold cuts (CHF 10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy groceries tonight to save money on breakfasts all week. Consider purchasing a Jungfrau Travel Pass or Grindelwald ski pass in advance online for better rates. Confirm accommodation check-in time before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: First full ski day! Head to Grindelwald–First ski area, one of the most accessible and family-friendly ski zones in the Jungfrau Region. Take the First Gondola from the village (included in Jungfrau ski pass). Beginners and families can enjoy gentle blue runs while more experienced skiers tackle red runs. Ski school sessions for kids available at the First ski school (book in advance for discounts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First plateau. Try the famous First Cliff Walk by Tissot — a free scenic mountain walkway with dramatic cliff-edge views (accessible even in ski boots). Pack a picnic lunch to eat at the mountain terrace and save on expensive mountain restaurant prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a local café. Visit the Grindelwald Sports & Leisure Center (Sportzentrum) for a swim or sauna session to relax tired muscles (entry ~CHF 10–15).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — muesli, bread, cheese, and fruit from yesterday's grocery run (CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch prepared at the hotel — sandwiches, fruit, thermos of hot tea (CHF 3–5 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — casual Swiss comfort food, rösti and sausages, budget-friendly portions (CHF 18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment in the village rather than at the mountain — rental shops like Intersport Grindelwald offer better rates (approx. CHF 30–40/day for full kit). Book ski passes online in advance for up to 10–15% savings. Dress in warm layers — February temperatures at altitude can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Jungfrau Railway from Grindelwald Grund station up to Kleine Scheidegg (included in Jungfrau Travel Pass or ~CHF 20–30 return). Ski the famous Lauberhorn ski runs — the same slopes used for the World Cup downhill race. This area is excellent for intermediate skiers and offers breathtaking views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing around Wengen side or try the long Grindelwald–Grund run back down to the valley (one of the longest ski runs in the region at ~5 km). Alternatively, if traveling with young children, take a family-friendly sledding run near Kleine Scheidegg — rent sleds at the station (CHF 5–10).
day_by_day.evening: Back in Grindelwald village, visit the free Grindelwald Museum (open select evenings) to learn about local alpine history and culture. Stroll the illuminated village streets after dark — magical in winter.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — eggs, bread, jam, and yogurt (CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Kleine Scheidegg has a self-service restaurant — opt for soup and bread (CHF 10–14 per person) or bring packed lunch
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Avocado in Grindelwald — wood-fired pizzas and pasta at reasonable prices (CHF 16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lauberhorn area can get busy mid-week in peak February season — start early (lifts open 8:30 AM) to avoid queues. Kleine Scheidegg is at 2,061 m elevation — apply sunscreen even in winter as UV rays are intense on snow. Keep children hydrated as altitude can cause mild fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' (3,454 m). Take the Jungfrau Railway from Grindelwald Grund via Kleine Scheidegg. Book tickets in advance online for the best price (Good Morning Ticket available before 8:30 AM is significantly cheaper — approx. CHF 145 vs CHF 185 standard). Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and snow plateau at the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Jungfraujoch, try snow tubing and snow disc activities on the plateau (free with entry). Walk the Alpine Sensation tunnel exhibit. Take memorable family photos with the stunning glacier views. Begin descent back to Grindelwald by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the accommodation after the high-altitude excursion. Cook a simple dinner together using groceries — a great family bonding activity and major budget saver.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at 6:30 AM to catch the Good Morning Train (bread, instant oats, fruit — CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch to eat at Jungfraujoch — sandwiches, chocolate, thermos of soup. Restaurant at the top is very expensive (CHF 25–40/meal). Bring snacks.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — pasta with tomato sauce, salad, and Swiss cheese (CHF 8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Good Morning Ticket to Jungfraujoch is the single best budget tip for this visit — saves CHF 30–40 per person. Book weeks in advance as slots fill up. Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454 m — ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid overexertion. Children under 16 travel at reduced rates. Bring sunglasses and sunscreen — snow glare is extreme.

day_by_day.morning: Try a different winter sport: snowshoeing! Rent snowshoes in Grindelwald village (CHF 10–15/day) and follow the free, well-marked Grindelwald snowshoe trail toward Bachalpsee lake (approx. 3–4 km each way). The frozen lake surrounded by snow-covered peaks is one of the most photogenic spots in the Alps. Suitable for families with children aged 6+.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village and visit the Grindelwald Adventure Park or try the village ice skating rink at the Sportzentrum (entry ~CHF 6–10, skate rental ~CHF 5). Ice skating is a perfect family activity and very budget-friendly compared to ski passes. Alternatively, take a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the village outskirts (CHF 20–30 per sled, shared).
day_by_day.evening: Fondue night! Buy a fondue kit from Coop/Migros (CHF 15–20 for a set serving 2–3 people) and enjoy a traditional Swiss cheese fondue in your accommodation. This is a quintessential Swiss Alps experience done on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — Swiss muesli with milk, fruit, and coffee/tea (CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches for the snowshoe trail — eat at Bachalpsee with a view (CHF 3–5 per person)
meals.dinner: Self-catered fondue night at accommodation — Gruyère and Emmental cheese fondue with bread and pickles from supermarket (CHF 8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The trail to Bachalpsee can be icy — wear proper hiking boots or snowshoes and use trekking poles if available. Check trail conditions at the Grindelwald tourist office (free service). The fondue kit from Coop is excellent value and includes the fondue set, cheese mix, and instructions — a highlight of the trip for families.

day_by_day.morning: Final ski day — head back to Grindelwald–First for any runs you haven't yet tried. Alternatively, try the First Flyer zipline (CHF 23 per ride) — a thrilling 800-meter zipline over the alpine terrain, great for older kids and adults. First also offers the First Glider (4-person glider experience, CHF 29) for a unique bird's-eye view of the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely ski or snowshoe down to Bort and Grindel stations, enjoying the lower mountain terrain. Visit the free Grindelwald Sports Museum near the gondola base. Spend the afternoon doing any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for Swiss chocolate, postcards, and small cowbells at the Coop or local shops (much cheaper than tourist boutiques).
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final dinner out at a local restaurant. Treat yourselves to a proper Swiss meal — raclette or rösti with bratwurst.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, bread, Swiss cheese, and juice (CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Mountain self-service café at First — soup, hot drinks, and a shared portion of fries (CHF 12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter Grindelwald — known for good value Swiss and international dishes, lively atmosphere (CHF 20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes as weekend visitors arrive from Zurich and Bern — head to the lifts early (by 8:30 AM) to beat queues. The First Flyer and Glider have minimum age/height requirements — check the Grindelwald–First website before booking. Buy Swiss chocolate at Coop/Migros for gifts — same quality as boutique shops at half the price.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Grindelwald. Take a relaxed walk through the village one last time, soaking in the alpine atmosphere. Visit the Grindelwald Parish Church (free) — a beautiful traditional Swiss church with mountain backdrop, perfect for photos. Enjoy a slow breakfast and begin packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation (standard checkout 11:00 AM — ask to store luggage if needed). Take the train from Grindelwald to Interlaken Ost, then connect to Zurich Airport. The journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours — enjoy the scenic Bernese Oberland views from the train window one last time. Arrive at Zurich Airport with ample time for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Grab a final Swiss treat — a Läderach or Lindt chocolate bar from the airport duty-free as a souvenir (CHF 5–15).

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast — finish remaining groceries: bread, jam, cheese, fruit, and hot drinks (CHF 2–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks for the train journey — leftover snacks, chocolate, and drinks from the week (CHF 3–5 per person) OR a quick meal at Interlaken Ost station café (CHF 10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Zurich Airport or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains are extremely punctual — arrive at Grindelwald station at least 10 minutes before departure. Validate your ticket before boarding. If you have a Swiss Travel Pass, it covers the full journey to the airport. Recycle any unused ski rental gear before checkout to avoid late fees. Keep train tickets and receipts for any travel insurance claims.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore the legendary Jungfrau ski region with guided family ski runs across Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. Includes beginner-friendly slopes for kids and intermediate runs for adults, with stunning views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.

experiences.description: Family ice skating session on a natural frozen alpine lake followed by an introduction to curling led by local Swiss instructors. A quintessential Swiss winter experience suitable for all ages and skill levels.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Grindelwald (approx. 2–2.5 hours via train from Zurich or Geneva). Settle into the Grindelwald Boutique Stay, unpack, and get oriented with the resort village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings. Visit the local ski rental shops to arrange equipment for the week ahead. Pick up ski passes and confirm bookings. Explore the village center and admire views of the Eiger North Face.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a cozy local restaurant in Grindelwald. Try traditional Swiss Rösti and Raclette to kick off the trip in style.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Zurich/Geneva airport or a train station café en route — try a Swiss pretzel and coffee
meals.dinner: Restaurant Alte Post Grindelwald — mid-range Alpine dining with Raclette, Rösti, and local craft beer; budget approx. CHF 35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau Travel Pass or Top Ski Region pass upon arrival at Grindelwald train station to save money on lifts and transport throughout the week. Confirm ski rental reservation for Day 2 morning. Dress warmly — Grindelwald sits at 1,034m elevation and February temperatures average -4°C to 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Ski Safari — Day 1: Join the guided Jungfrau Ski Safari experience starting from Grindelwald First ski area. A certified ski guide leads the family through beginner and intermediate runs on Grindelwald's wide, groomed pistes. The safari covers scenic routes with breathtaking views of the Wetterhorn and Schreckhorn peaks. Ski lessons available for younger or less experienced family members.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Jungfrau Ski Safari across to the Kleine Scheidegg area, connecting Grindelwald with Wengen via the famous ski runs. Take the Jungfraubahn cogwheel railway for a scenic mid-afternoon break and enjoy panoramic alpine views. Optional: ride up toward Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe) if time and budget allow (approx. CHF 145 adult with pass discount).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by ski or train. Warm up with Glühwein (mulled wine) at an après-ski bar in the village before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Boutique Stay breakfast or a local bakery — fresh croissants, Swiss cheese, cold cuts, and coffee; budget CHF 10–15
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Kleine Scheidegg — hearty soup, bread, and hot chocolate; budget CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Memory Grindelwald — mid-range Swiss cuisine featuring fondue and seasonal specials; budget CHF 40–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book ski school for children in advance through the Swiss Ski School Grindelwald (online or at the resort). Wear SPF 50+ sunscreen — UV radiation is significantly stronger at altitude. Helmet rental strongly recommended for all family members.

day_by_day.morning: Interlaken Ice Skating & Curling on Lake Brienz — Take the scenic train from Grindelwald to Interlaken (approx. 35 minutes). Head to Lake Brienz for a family ice skating session on the natural frozen alpine lake. Glide across the ice surrounded by snow-capped mountains in a magical winter setting. Skate rentals available on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introduction to curling on Lake Brienz — a fun, competitive family activity with an instructor explaining the basics of this classic Swiss winter sport. Teams compete in a friendly mini-tournament. Afterward, explore Interlaken's charming Höheweg promenade and browse Swiss souvenir shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the boutique stay or nearby spa if the hotel offers wellness facilities.

meals.breakfast: Boutique Stay breakfast — Swiss muesli, yogurt, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Café in Interlaken near the lake — try a Swiss cheese sandwich (Käseschnitten) and hot soup; budget CHF 18–25 per person
meals.dinner: Onkel Tom's Hütte Grindelwald — popular mid-range restaurant with pizzas, pastas, and Swiss dishes; family-friendly atmosphere; budget CHF 30–45 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check lake ice conditions in advance — the activity operator will confirm if the natural lake is frozen solid enough (usually reliable in February). Interlaken is a short, easy train ride and a great change of scenery. Bring hand warmers for the children during the ice activities.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Ski Safari — Day 2: Return to the slopes for the second leg of the Jungfrau Ski Safari, this time exploring the Männlichen and Grindelwald-Grund areas. The guide takes the family on more adventurous intermediate runs with stunning views across the Lauterbrunnen Valley. This is one of the most scenic ski descents in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free ski afternoon on Grindelwald First — families can explore the terrain at their own pace. Older kids and adults can try the Scooter Snow Bikes available for rent on the First plateau, while younger children can enjoy the dedicated kids' snow park. Take the First Cliff Walk (accessible in winter) for dramatic cliff-edge views.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at Bargrill Grindelwald followed by a special family fondue dinner — a quintessential Swiss Alps experience.

meals.breakfast: Boutique Stay breakfast — eggs, cold cuts, cheese, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant First — panoramic mountain restaurant with daily specials, soup, and Schnitzel; budget CHF 25–35 per person
meals.dinner: Fondue evening at Chalet-Hotel Gletschergarten Grindelwald — traditional cheese and meat fondue set menus; budget CHF 45–60 per person including wine/soft drinks

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is a great mid-trip day to push skiing skills further. Consider booking a private ski lesson for the afternoon if any family member wants to progress faster. Fondue dinner reservations should be made at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Swiss Chocolate Workshop — Travel by train from Grindelwald to Davos (approx. 2.5–3 hours via Interlaken and Chur). Begin the morning with a guided cross-country skiing session along the groomed trails of the Davos valley. The flat and rolling terrain is perfect for families and beginners. Glide through pristine snow-covered pine forests with the crisp Alpine air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Chocolate Workshop in Davos — warm up indoors with a hands-on Swiss chocolate-making workshop. Learn the art of tempering chocolate, create your own truffles and pralines, and take home your handmade creations. A huge hit with children and adults alike. Explore Davos Platz briefly before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Grindelwald (arrive approx. 19:30–20:00). Light dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — packed or quick continental
meals.lunch: Café or mountain hut along the cross-country ski trail in Davos — try Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and bread; budget CHF 20–28 per person
meals.dinner: Café 3692 Grindelwald or hotel restaurant — light dinner of soup, salad, and pasta after the long travel day; budget CHF 25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Davos day trip is long but very rewarding — it adds variety to the week beyond Grindelwald. Book train tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) app for best prices. The chocolate workshop must be pre-booked online. Bring the Jungfrau Travel Pass for potential rail discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Snow Tubing & Sledding Adventure — Take the early train from Grindelwald toward Zermatt (approx. 2.5 hours via Visp). Head up to Riffelberg by the Gornergrat railway for a thrilling family snow tubing and sledding session on Zermatt's famous sledding runs. The runs offer spectacular views of the Matterhorn — one of the most iconic mountain scenes in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore car-free Zermatt village on foot — browse the charming streets, visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis), and take photos of the iconic Matterhorn from the village. Optional: take the Gornergrat railway up to 3,089m for breathtaking panoramic views of 29 four-thousand-meter peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zermatt before taking the evening train back to Grindelwald (arrive approx. 21:30). Alternatively, enjoy a final glass of Glühwein in Zermatt before departure.

meals.breakfast: Boutique Stay breakfast — full spread before the early departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant Riffelberg (mid-mountain) — mountain cuisine with Matterhorn views; try Alpine macaroni or beef goulash; budget CHF 30–45 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Whymper-Stube Zermatt — famous mid-range restaurant in Zermatt serving fondue and Swiss classics; budget CHF 40–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — only electric taxis and horse-drawn sleighs operate in the village, which adds to the magical atmosphere. Book Gornergrat railway tickets in advance online for a discount. The sledding run at Riffelberg (5km long) is one of the best in Switzerland — helmets are provided. This is a highlight day of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Snowshoeing & Alpine Fondue Experience — For the final full morning, take a shorter local alternative: join a guided snowshoeing tour in the Grindelwald area (Grindelwald offers its own snowshoe trails as an accessible local alternative to traveling to Verbier, saving travel time on the last day). Explore pristine alpine meadows and pine forests above the village on snowshoes, guided by a local mountain guide. Suitable for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Alpine Fondue lunch at a mountain hut following the snowshoe trek — the perfect farewell to the Swiss Alps. After lunch, return to Grindelwald for final packing, souvenir shopping in the village, and checking out of the boutique stay. Pick up Swiss chocolates, cheese, and local gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Grindelwald village. Reflect on an incredible week in the Alps with a special celebratory meal.

meals.breakfast: Boutique Stay final breakfast — enjoy the full spread one last time
meals.lunch: Alpine fondue at a mountain hut post-snowshoe trek — cheese fondue with bread, charcuterie, and hot drinks included in the experience package; budget CHF 35–50 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte Grindelwald — beloved local restaurant with panoramic Eiger views, serving Swiss classics and seasonal game dishes; budget CHF 45–60 per person for a celebratory farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Snowshoe rental is included in most guided tour packages — confirm with the local guide service. Buy Swiss chocolate and cheese at the Grindelwald Coop or local deli as take-home gifts. Confirm return transport arrangements to the airport for the following day if departing on Day 8.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Grindelwald is approximately 2.5–3 hours by private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Grindelwald Boutique Stay in the Jungfrau Region. Check-in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity (champagne, Swiss chocolates, warm towels). Take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to orient yourselves — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face and the snow-dusted chalets. Visit the local ski rental boutique to arrange premium equipment fitting for the family.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a top-rated local establishment. Enjoy a candlelit alpine dining experience featuring Swiss classics such as raclette, veal Zurich-style, and seasonal desserts. Early night to rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments during private transfer — pre-arranged charcuterie and Swiss cheese hamper in the vehicle
meals.dinner: The Eigerstübli or Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof Grindelwald — multi-course Swiss alpine cuisine with curated local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer in advance (Mercedes V-Class or similar). Confirm ski equipment rental and sizing appointments for Day 2. Ensure lift passes are pre-purchased for the Jungfrau Ski Region to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Ski Safari (Morning Session) — Join a certified private ski guide for an exclusive family ski experience across the legendary Jungfrau ski region. Start with groomed beginner-to-intermediate runs on Grindelwald First, enjoying panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. The guide tailors the pace and route to all family skill levels, ensuring a safe and exhilarating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Jungfrau Ski Safari into the afternoon — ski down to Wengen via the interconnected lift network, exploring varied terrain including wide cruising pistes and gentle tree-lined runs. Stop mid-slope at a mountain restaurant for a warm lunch with views. After skiing, return to Grindelwald by the Wengernalp Railway for a unique scenic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the hotel's lounge — warm up with Swiss mulled wine (Glühwein) and cheese fondue bites by the fireplace. Dinner at a premium Grindelwald restaurant featuring regional game, alpine herbs, and a curated Swiss wine list.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cold cuts, eggs to order, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on-piste — Bergrestaurant Männlichen or Restaurant Grindelwald First; hearty rösti, alpine soup, and hot chocolate for the kids
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte Grindelwald — known for premium Swiss alpine cuisine, fondue, and an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book a private certified ski guide at least 48 hours in advance through the Swiss Ski School Grindelwald. Ensure all family members have properly fitted helmets and appropriate layering. Jungfrau lift passes cover Grindelwald, Wengen, Mürren, and Männlichen.

day_by_day.morning: Interlaken Ice Skating & Curling on Lake Brienz — Depart Grindelwald by private chauffeur (approximately 30 minutes) to Interlaken and Lake Brienz. Enjoy a magical family ice skating session on the naturally frozen alpine lake surrounded by snow-capped mountains. Premium ice skate rentals and warm-up gear are provided. A professional skating instructor accompanies beginners and younger children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introduction to Curling — transition to a dedicated curling lane on the lake or at a nearby indoor facility. A local curling coach leads a fun, competitive family session. Afterward, explore Interlaken's luxury boutiques along Höheweg promenade — pick up Swiss watches, premium chocolates from Läderach, and local souvenirs before returning to Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite or private dining room fondue experience at the hotel — a chef prepares a traditional Swiss cheese fondue and chocolate fondue dessert exclusively for your family, paired with local wines and sparkling grape juice for the children.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan breads, seasonal fruits, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Gasthof Hirschen in Interlaken or Restaurant du Lac — lakeside dining with fresh perch from Lake Brienz, seasonal vegetables, and Swiss-style desserts
meals.dinner: Private in-room or private dining room fondue experience arranged by the hotel's concierge — premium Gruyère and Appenzeller cheese fondue with charcuterie starters

day_by_day.notes: Check ice conditions on Lake Brienz in advance — the hotel concierge can confirm natural ice availability. If the lake is not frozen, the Interlaken Ice Rink (Kunsteisbahn) is an excellent indoor alternative. Private chauffeur transfer recommended for comfort and convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing — Depart early by private transfer to Davos (approximately 2 hours). Glide along the world-renowned 75 km network of groomed cross-country ski trails through the breathtaking Davos valley. A private Nordic ski instructor guides the family through the scenic Flüela and Dischma valley trails, suitable for all levels. Enjoy the serene alpine landscape away from the downhill ski crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Chocolate Workshop in Davos — warm up indoors at a premium Swiss chocolate atelier. A master chocolatier leads the family through the art of Swiss chocolate-making — tempering, molding, and decorating bespoke chocolate creations to take home as edible souvenirs. A truly hands-on and delightful experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by private transfer. Unwind with a spa session at the hotel — heated indoor pool, sauna, steam room, and optional family massage treatments. Light and elegant dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — grab-and-go premium hamper option available if departing before the buffet opens
meals.lunch: Davos mountain restaurant or Bergrestaurant Schatzalp — panoramic views, hearty alpine cuisine, local cheese platters, and warm soups
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or Restaurant Mercato Grindelwald — Italian-Swiss fusion cuisine with truffles, premium pastas, and alpine-inspired desserts

day_by_day.notes: Davos is approximately 2 hours from Grindelwald — depart by 7:30 AM to maximize time. Book the chocolate workshop in advance as spots are limited. Nordic ski equipment can be rented in Davos upon arrival. Return transfer should be pre-scheduled for approximately 17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Snowshoeing & Alpine Fondue Experience — Depart by private transfer to Verbier (approximately 2.5 hours). A certified mountain guide leads the family on a guided snowshoe trek through pristine alpine meadows, pine forests, and frozen streams above Verbier. The pace is family-friendly, with stops to observe winter wildlife tracks, frozen waterfalls, and breathtaking panoramas of the Mont Blanc massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Swiss Alpine Fondue Lunch — the snowshoe trek concludes at a remote, rustic mountain chalet where a local host prepares an authentic Swiss fondue experience with local cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and warm alpine herbal tea. Afterward, enjoy free time in Verbier village — explore the vibrant après-ski scene, luxury boutiques, and art galleries before the return transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald. Celebratory family dinner at one of Grindelwald's finest restaurants — a multi-course tasting menu showcasing the best of Swiss and Alpine cuisine, paired with a sommelier-curated wine flight for adults and artisan mocktails for children.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Swiss spread with regional specialties, fresh-pressed juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Included in the Verbier Snowshoeing & Alpine Fondue Experience — traditional fondue, raclette bites, charcuterie, and warm drinks at the alpine chalet
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firescue or The Capra Verbier (if staying late) — alternatively, Restaurant Alte Post Grindelwald upon return for a premium 5-course tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Verbier is a longer transfer — consider departing by 7:00 AM. Snowshoe equipment is provided by the guide. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, waterproof outer layers, and sturdy waterproof boots. The fondue chalet experience is weather-dependent — the guide will confirm the route the morning of the activity.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Snow Tubing & Sledding Adventure — Early private transfer to Zermatt (approximately 2.5 hours, car-free village entry via Täsch shuttle). Take the Gornergrat Bahn railway up to Riffelberg for a thrilling family snow tubing and sledding session on Zermatt's famous runs. The iconic Matterhorn provides an unforgettable backdrop. Kids and adults alike will love the adrenaline of the dedicated tubing lanes and natural sledding tracks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Zermatt village — visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) for a fascinating insight into alpine history and mountaineering heritage. Browse Zermatt's luxury boutiques for Swiss watches, cashmere, and premium sportswear. Optional: take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car to Europe's highest viewing platform at 3,883 m for panoramic views across four countries.
day_by_day.evening: Premium dinner in Zermatt before returning to Grindelwald. Zermatt boasts some of Switzerland's finest restaurants — indulge in a world-class dining experience before the private transfer back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs to order, smoked fish, artisan Swiss cheeses, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Riffelberg Restaurant Zermatt — elevated mountain dining with stunning Matterhorn views; enjoy Swiss-style beef tartare, alpine rösti, and seasonal desserts
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Vrony Zermatt (Findeln) or Restaurant Zum See — legendary Zermatt fine dining with locally sourced ingredients, exceptional wine lists, and impeccable mountain views

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — all vehicles must be parked in Täsch (free parking) with a short shuttle train into the village. Book Restaurant Chez Vrony or Zum See well in advance as they are extremely popular. The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car is weather-dependent — check conditions the morning of the visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in the Jungfrau Region — A leisurely final ski run or snowshoe walk directly from Grindelwald. Take the Grindelwald First gondola for one last breathtaking alpine panorama and a gentle family ski run or a relaxed walk on the First Cliff Walk — a spectacular suspended walkway with sheer drops and 360-degree mountain views. Collect any remaining ski equipment and return rentals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Grindelwald Boutique Stay. Enjoy a final Swiss lunch in Grindelwald village before the private luxury transfer back to the airport. Browse last-minute Swiss souvenirs — Läderach chocolates, Swiss army knives, and local cheese to take home. Depart for the airport with memories of an extraordinary alpine journey.
day_by_day.evening: Airport transfer and departure. If the flight is late evening, consider a farewell dinner at an airport lounge or a premium restaurant in Zurich or Geneva city center.

meals.breakfast: Extended farewell hotel breakfast — take your time with a full Swiss spread, celebrating the final morning in the Alps
meals.lunch: Restaurant Grindelwald First Summit or Café 3692 — final alpine lunch with panoramic views, Swiss specialties, and warm drinks
meals.dinner: Airport lounge premium dining or, if time permits, Restaurant Kronenhalle Zurich or Brasserie Lipp Geneva — iconic Swiss fine dining for a memorable farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport and 3 hours to Geneva Airport for check-in and security. Arrange private luxury transfer the evening before to confirm timing. The hotel concierge can assist with luggage shipping (Swiss Post Fly Luggage service) directly to the airport if needed — a premium convenience worth arranging.
